sources.name: Incident Metrics in SRE — Štěpán Davidovič (Google SRE / O'Reilly)
sources.notes: Sparse, high-variance samples undermine means, medians and high-percentile trend estimates. Printed pp. 14–15 and 24–28; measure the response step a change targets, with uncertainty. Does not prescribe percentiles as a universal replacement.

sources.name: Alerting on SLOs — Google SRE Workbook
sources.notes: Source for burn-rate thresholds: '2% budget consumption in one hour and 5% budget consumption in six hours as reasonable starting numbers for paging.' Used in references/slo-incident-triggering.md.

sources.name: Howie Post-Incident Guide — PagerDuty
sources.notes: Open standard for structured post-incident review. Covers narrative framing, structured interviews, near-miss inclusion, and human-factors lens. Added to references/postmortem-facilitation.md as the named standard for SEV1/SEV2 reviews.

sources.name: Google SRE Incident Management Guide
sources.notes: Google SRE end-to-end incident management process grounded in incident command and operational readiness.

sources.name: Google SRE Anatomy of an Incident
sources.notes: Lifecycle framing for preparedness, response, recovery, and mitigation.

sources.name: Atlassian Incident Management Handbook
sources.notes: Incident-management operating model covering severity, coordination, communication, and learning loops.

sources.name: PagerDuty Incident Response Documentation
sources.notes: Open-sourced PagerDuty incident response process covering before, during, and after an incident.

sources.name: PagerDuty During an Incident
sources.notes: Operational guidance for major incident execution, coordination, and documentation.

sources.name: PagerDuty Severity Levels
sources.notes: Severity model guidance for response expectations and escalation policy.

sources.name: DORA incident reporting — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301
sources.notes: Article 5 defines awareness/classification timing, the late-classification rule, submission-anchored intermediate/final deadlines, and holiday exceptions. Incident templates are in ITS 2025/302, not ITS 2024/2956.

sources.name: NIS2 Directive Article 23 — Reporting obligations
sources.notes: Article 23: awareness-triggered staged reporting; trust-service-provider exception and progress/final-report handling for ongoing incidents. Confirm national implementing law and CSIRT instructions.

sources.name: SEC Item 1.05 Form 8-K cybersecurity incident disclosure
sources.notes: Item 1.05 applies to domestic registrants; the materiality determination, without unreasonable delay, starts its filing clock. Foreign private issuers follow Form 6-K. Counsel confirms scope and permitted delays.

sources.name: DORA incident reporting forms — Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/302
sources.notes: Standard forms, templates and procedures for major ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats. Annex I supplies the incident template.
